title: Reduce excessive constructor/method parameters using options pattern
description:
## Source
SonarQube static analysis audit (`Data/Pages/audits/ms-sonar-static-analysis-7-26-26.md`)

## Findings
17 constructors/methods with parameter counts exceeding the recommended limit of 7:

**Worst offenders (10+ parameters):**
- `ChatServices.cs` L1731 — 12 params
- `SecurityServices.cs` L942 — 12 params
- `CodeSearchService.cs` L2503 — 11 params
- `AgentSessionService.cs` L114 — 11 params
- `MemoryApplicationService.cs` L58 — 11 params
- `SecurityServices.cs` L909 — 10 params

**Other (8-9 params):**
- `Admin.razor` L3161 (8), `McpController.cs` L35 (9), `AgentSessionService.cs` L145 (9), `ChatModelProfileService.cs` L197 (8), `CodeSearchService.cs` L812 (9), L2494 (8), L2497 (8), L2500 (8), `MaintenanceAgentServices.cs` L1288 (8), `MemoryChatAgent.ToolLoop.cs` L66 (8), `SecurityServices.cs` L133 (9)

## Impact
High parameter counts make constructors hard to use and test, violating the Single Responsibility Principle by implying the class has too many dependencies.

## Action Required
Introduce parameter objects or options classes. For constructors, use the options pattern (`IOptions<T>`). Group related parameters into dedicated `sealed record` types. Consider facade/service decomposition for classes with >10 dependencies.

## Effort
~5h40min

## Priority
P1 — Design/Refactor
